employment_method.permanent_jobs: Operation and maintenance, fuel supply/handling, and desalination employment. Reported as ongoing annual jobs.
employment_method.temporary_jobs: Local and export manufacturing, construction and installation, and electricity and water transmission. Reported as job-years, not permanent positions.

emissions.unit: million tonnes CO2 (as reported in thesis; not a complete lifecycle GHG inventory)
emissions.non_co2_note: The thesis states that total CO2-equivalent emissions including CH4, N2O and fluorinated gases are not fully eliminated by 2050; leakage and non-CO2 emissions remain concerns. The reported negative e-methane balance reflects the thesis accounting allocation of captured CO2 to importing countries, not a full lifecycle assessment.

limitations: Employment figures are modelled estimates based on technology employment factors, investment assumptions and adjustment multipliers; they are not guaranteed jobs or observed employment.
Permanent jobs are annual ongoing positions; temporary employment is measured in job-years. These units must not be added together or presented as equivalent.
The desalination employment intensity is stated to be valid only up to plant capacity of 150 million m3/year; the thesis cautions that scaling to larger future plants makes predictions less reliable.

Water-demand totals are copied from thesis Table 13. The table's formatting places energy-use TWh values alongside water-use Gm3 values; this dataset keeps only the Gm3 water quantities and does not reinterpret the TWh rows as water.
The 2050 water-access figures are scenario targets/projections, not measured outcomes. The thesis describes more than 6,838 km of planned pipelines and 80% desalination coverage.

Solar land estimates use the thesis assumptions: 20% panel efficiency, 0.84 system efficiency, 0.24 capacity factor and 0.6 ground coverage ratio. They estimate PV land only, not all project infrastructure or ecological disturbance.

The thesis characterises Site 02 as sparsely populated with low ecological activity, but land occupation may still affect grazing, mobility, livelihoods and cultural practices. Local consultation and fair benefit-sharing are necessary.

The emissions results are thesis accounting outputs, not independently verified lifecycle emissions. The negative e-methane balance depends on the thesis treatment of captured CO2 and importing-country offsets.
